Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports combining sequence encoding with global interaction graphs. [GaGNN (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002002552400536X) models individual and group transitions with separate sequential/collaborative encoders and information fusion. [TGCL4SR (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) combines a global temporal item-transition graph with a local Transformer, using neighbor sampling, temporal perturbations, and contrastive learning. [LS4SRec (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3723173) uses a weighted global item-transition graph to supply collaborative signals while separating long- and short-term interests. These papers motivate recovering cross-user associations that sparse individual histories cannot reliably reveal; they do not establish gains on this pinned RecHarness benchmark.

Practical inference for this task: retain SASRec and test a complementary ranking branch built exclusively from training histories—directed transition counts plus normalized item co-occurrence neighborhoods, aggregated over recent history with recency weights. Tune score normalization and blending on macro validation HR@10; compare against each branch alone. This lightweight blend is an experimental proposal, not a reported result from those papers. Text is optional: [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) investigates titles, descriptions, and reviews, but its setting does not establish a compliant, trained-from-scratch recipe here. A small randomly initialized token encoder over available titles/descriptions is a reasonable ablation; exclude reviews and external pretrained representations. Prioritize interaction-only neighborhoods first to determine whether complementary ranking evidence helps before spending budget on text or graph neural training.

---

Recent research supports separating persistent preferences from recent intent and learning their relative importance. [TLSTSRec (2024/2025)](https://doi.org/10.3233/ida-240051) combines temporal representations with adaptive long/short-term fusion. [HM4SR (WWW 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14269) introduces interactive and temporal mixtures of experts, explicit timestamp embeddings, and auxiliary contrastive objectives targeting sparsity. Its multimodal inputs and category-prediction supervision exceed this benchmark’s available data; temporal routing and ID-based contrastive learning are transferable hypotheses.

Two 2026 directions sharpen the design. [MGUI](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11506283) combines time-interval gating for individual recent items, group-level interest modeling, cross-user transition graphs, and user-specific expert weighting. [MIMAR-SRec (AAAI 2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) models intent across contextual windows, with contrastive alignment and robustness against interaction, temporal, and preference noise. These papers motivate multiple temporal views, but do not establish gains on the pinned RecHarness evaluation.

A practical experiment inferred from these approaches: retain SASRec, add pooled historical-interest and recent-window branches, then gate their contributions using sequence length, observed time gaps, and branch representations. Compare fixed fusion, learned fusion, and timestamp-conditioned fusion; inspect performance by history length and gap size, alongside expert utilization. Start with a small gate because sparse histories provide limited routing evidence. Treat inferred intent transitions, satisfied needs, and compatibility as latent hypotheses—not observed labels—and select changes solely by macro validation HR@10.

---

Evidence supports investigating weak ranking despite good training separation. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024; original RecSys 2023)](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes SASRec degradation to overconfidence under sampled BCE and proposes generalized BCE. This supports a loss/sampling ablation, but does not establish that multi-negative sampled softmax will win on these four categories. A [2024 negative-sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity-bias tradeoffs across random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling.

Hardness should be controlled. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) reports that introducing hard negatives too early can harm learning; it uses uniform warm-start followed by curriculum mining. Highest-scoring unobserved items may be false negatives; stochastic selection among several high-ranked candidates reduces deterministic selection risk. Practical experiment, inferred from this evidence: compare single-negative BCE, multi-negative BCE/gBCE and sampled softmax with 16–64 uniform negatives, then introduce a small hard-negative fraction after warm-up. Mask known training positives; never inspect held-out labels to filter negatives. Score bounded candidate pools rather than mining the full catalog at every update.

## Starting Research Idea
SASRec encodes interaction histories using learned item and position embeddings, causal self-attention, and feed-forward blocks. It ranks candidate items by dot products with the final history representation. Training uses next-item binary cross-entropy with sampled negatives. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
